speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe how the lesion started, such as whether it was a bite or trauma, and how long it has been present? I also need to know if you have any underlying medical conditions like diabetes or vascular disease.

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and diabetes, I need to rule out an inflammatory condition like erythema nodosum or a diabetic ulcer. Have you experienced any joint pain, fever, or gastrointestinal symptoms recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The purplish irregular borders and central necrosis following an insect bite are highly suggestive of pyoderma gangrenosum, especially given your history of Crohn's disease. To confirm this diagnosis and rule out infection, I will order a wound culture and a biopsy of the lesion edge.
